investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, meaning the VM slot quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of scheduling. The remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, making them ineligible. Preemption was also ruled out: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) timed out after ~130 s without writing any evidence, causing a complete contract gap for all four required fields. This is an eval-layer signal of a real infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm slot exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, so any capacity problem on those nodes produces a total scheduling failure across all 6 nodes. The 4 non-matching nodes cannot serve as fallback.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods consuming VM slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, reducing available capacity below what is needed for new probe pods.

Lower confidence — node-level resource pressure or node NotReady on the 2 kata nodes: if either kata node is under memory/CPU pressure or temporarily NotReady, the extended resource count reported to the scheduler could be reduced, causing apparent exhaustion even if slots are nominally available.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion — Pods Unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-02 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) before it can poll state, the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the two eligible nodes. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every pod submitted by the eval runner (and by extension any real remote-agent creation request routed through the same cluster) is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. The eval runner never reaches the state-polling phase, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is absent and the check fails. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api cluster, not an application code defect.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4/6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or a node label was removed, effective capacity is artificially reduced.

TERTIARY — VM quota or peer-pod provider limit reached at the infrastructure layer (e.g., cloud provider VM quota, peer-pod controller limit): the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is typically managed by a peer-pod controller; if that controller's upstream quota is exhausted, it stops advertising capacity and nodes report Insufficient.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Swarm Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, meaning the VM slot quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of scheduling. The remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, making them ineligible. Preemption was also ruled out: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) timed out after ~130 s without writing any evidence, causing a complete contract gap for all four required fields. This is an eval-layer signal of a real infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=148325, no evidence keys — same root cause reproduced on a third independent pod.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be satisfied without a running pod.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm slot exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, so any capacity problem on those nodes produces a total scheduling failure across all 6 nodes. The 4 non-matching nodes cannot serve as fallback.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods consuming VM slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, reducing available capacity below what is needed for new probe pods.

Lower confidence — node-level resource pressure or node NotReady on the 2 kata nodes: if either kata node is under memory/CPU pressure or temporarily NotReady, the extended resource count reported to the scheduler could be reduced, causing apparent exhaustion even if slots are nominally available.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion — Pods Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-02 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) before it can poll state, the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots across the two eligible nodes. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every pod submitted by the eval runner (and by extension any real remote-agent creation request routed through the same cluster) is stuck in Pending/Unschedulable state. The eval runner never reaches the state-polling phase, so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is absent and the check fails. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool in the production-api cluster, not an application code defect.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes and no preemption victims exist, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4/6 nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity rules, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto only 2 nodes. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or a node label was removed, effective capacity is artificially reduced.

TERTIARY — VM quota or peer-pod provider limit reached at the infrastructure layer (e.g., cloud provider VM quota, peer-pod controller limit): the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is typically managed by a peer-pod controller; if that controller's upstream quota is exhausted, it stops advertising capacity and nodes report Insufficient.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Depleted Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 12:24 and 12:29 UTC on 2026-07-02 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had 0 available slots for new remote agent pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes rejecting the pod due to node affinity/selector mismatch. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was returned to satisfy the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector for remote agent pods. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to create a remote agent pod times out unscheduled (~130–148 s), preventing the eval runner from reaching the agent creation, state polling, or runtime chat steps. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new scheduling attempts. Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes also lost their kata.peerpods.io/vm label or capacity annotation, the effective schedulable pool would be 0. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

TERTIARY — Preemption policy prevents recovery: the scheduler found no preemption victims on the 2 eligible nodes and determined preemption is not helpful for the 4 non-matching nodes, meaning the cluster cannot self-heal without external intervention. Supported by 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' in failed-check.message.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Transient spike in concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously: a burst of user or system-initiated remote agents could have temporarily saturated capacity. No traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm this.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime without any scheduling changes would suggest the failure was transient (e.g., a momentary capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.

kubectl describe on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes showing available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity greater than zero at the time of the failure would disprove the exhaustion hypothesis and point instead to a scheduler bug or misconfigured resource request on the pod spec.
Evidence that the 4 non-matching nodes previously matched the affinity/selector and recently lost their labels would shift the primary cause from capacity exhaustion to node label drift.

A passing run of local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) at the same time would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote agent VM scheduling layer and not a broader cluster or API outage.

User-traffic or incident signals showing remote agent provisioning succeeding for end users during the same window would confirm this is an eval-only infrastructure issue rather than a user-facing outage.
